item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00399","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C05","C24","C06"],"selected_candidate_label":"C05","confidence":0.94,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C05 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both memoranda open by withholding approval of a private claims bill, describe a specific payment in full settlement, emphasize that the claim has already received repeated judicial consideration, and conclude that no equitable basis justifies overriding the courts through special legislation. C24 has a similar court-rejection/equitable-relief structure, while C06 shares the warning that exceptional relief would encourage analogous claims, but neither matches the child's factual and argumentative sequence as closely as C05.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"directing the payment of $581,721.91 to the State of Washington as full satisfaction of a claim against the United States","parent_excerpt":"authorizes and directs the Secretary of the Treasury to pay to Carl Piowaty and W. J. Piowaty the sum of $4,450 in full settlement of their claim against the United States","explanation":"Distinctively parallel description of a private bill directing a specified payment in full satisfaction or settlement of a claim against the United States."},{"child_excerpt":"The claim involved in the bill has been thoroughly litigated and its payment denied by judicial determination.","parent_excerpt":"The claims of the United States against these two persons and their claims against the United States have been adjudicated in the courts where both sides were afforded an opportunity to present all pertinent evidence","explanation":"Both make prior judicial adjudication the central reason Congress should not grant special relief."},{"child_excerpt":"Both the United States District Court ... and the United States Court of Appeals ... found ... The State was therefore not entitled to compensation. Certiorari was denied.","parent_excerpt":"The case was tried ... and a judgment was obtained ... They appealed ... where the lower court's judgment was sustained ... Appeal for a rehearing was thereafter denied.","explanation":"The child follows the parent's sequence of trial-court disposition, appellate affirmance, and denial of further review."},{"child_excerpt":"No equitable reason for overruling the decision of the courts has been advanced.","parent_excerpt":"In the light of this history of repeated judicial review, I cannot agree that Carl Piowaty and W. J. Piowaty should be given the special consideration and relief which the bill would provide.","explanation":"Closely parallel conclusion that repeated judicial review leaves no justification for exceptional legislative relief."}]}
